questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull to the shoulder and wait for the rain to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Roads are slippery when rain first starts, especially in the center of the lane. It is safest to ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles. The left tire track is often the best choice.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between you and other drivers?

options.text: At intersections.
On open highways.
On rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other traffic. Always use extra caution when approaching or going through an intersection.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy for safe riding. What does SEE stand for?

options.text: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
Slow, Experienced, and Error-free.
Safe, Experienced, and Evasive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
questions.explanation: Good riders use the SEE strategy to make safe decisions. SEE stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. This is safest. Riding on the side closest to the passing driver increases the risk of a collision. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to pull back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Signal ahead.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic or pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: If bright sunlight makes it hard for drivers to see your turn signals, what should you do?

options.text: Continue to use the mechanical turn signals.
Honk your horn to alert drivers of upcoming turns.
Use hand signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use hand signals.
questions.explanation: Use hand signals when bright sunlight makes your turn signals hard to see. It is very important to clearly tell other drivers what you are doing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, which part of the lane should you use?

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, the center of the lane is the safest position. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: Do you need hearing protection when riding?

options.text: No, a helmet is enough protection.
Only on long trips.
Yes, on all rides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, on all rides.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear hearing protection on every ride.

questions.question: What does your steering feel like if your front tire goes flat?

options.text: Heavy.
Loose.
Soft.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy.
questions.explanation: If steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: Which of these surfaces can be slippery?

options.text: A gravel road
A paved driveway
Dry pavement

questions.correctAnswerText: A gravel road
questions.explanation: Gravel roads, wet pavement, snow, ice, mud, lane markings, steel plates, and utility hole covers all have poor traction.

questions.question: When riding near a truck, what should you remember?

options.text: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
You should focus on riding and not worry about the truck's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding in trucks' blind spots. If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle passenger do?

options.text: Put their feet on the ground when the motorcycle is stopped.
Not ride without a back rest.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver.
questions.explanation: A passenger should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver. Keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: What is a good lane position?

options.text: It helps you see others and lets them see you.
It places you in other drivers' blind spots.
It invites others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you see others and lets them see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It also helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards. It discourages sharing and gives you an escape route.

questions.question: When can a motorcycle pass on the right?

options.text: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
By riding on the shoulder of the road.
By riding on the grass if it is level.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right if there is at least eight feet of clear pavement to the right of the vehicle being passed. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Which is NOT important when choosing riding clothes?

options.text: The clothing protects you from heat and cold.
The clothing makes you more visible to others.
The clothing does not leave weird tan lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: The clothing does not leave weird tan lines.
questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you from injury in a crash and make you more visible. They also protect you from heat, cold, road debris, and hot motorcycle parts.

questions.question: What is the safest part of the lane?

options.text: Always the left side.
Always the right side.
It depends on the situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on the situation.

questions.question: What is true about the center of the lane?

options.text: It should always be avoided.
It has oil and grease but usually provides enough grip for safe riding.
Other drivers cannot usually see you there.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has oil and grease but usually provides enough grip for safe riding.
questions.explanation: Car drippings build up in the center of lanes as an oily strip. This area usually provides enough traction for safe riding, unless it is wet.

questions.question: A plastic face shield protects you from:

options.text: Noise.
Dust.
Glare.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dust.
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your face in a crash. It also protects against pebbles, wind, dust, dirt, rain, and insects.

questions.question: How do you shift to a higher gear?

options.text: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift.
Place your foot over the shift lever and push.
Use your thumb to move the lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift.
questions.explanation: To shift up to a higher gear, put your foot under the shift lever and lift.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you arrive at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to tell the other vehicle to go.
Go through the intersection and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, what should the following distance be?

options.text: Increase.
Decrease.
Stay the same as normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle towing a trailer needs more stopping distance. The trailer's weight means the motorcycle takes longer to stop.

questions.question: If another driver makes eye contact with you, what does it mean?

options.text: They have definitely seen you.
It does not always mean they have actually seen you.
They will yield to you properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not always mean they have actually seen you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume a driver has seen you just because they made eye contact. A driver can look directly at you and still not notice you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel under 25 mph. Examples include construction equipment, farm machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.
